Discussing feature flag architectures, a Block/Square engineer said local in-memory evaluation should be standard, but noted 'flagsmith apparently does primarily server-side eval.' Another commenter replied that if so, 'flag evaluation can't possibly be part of any kind of hot loop.'

A user spent a day evaluating self-hosted feature flag tools (Java/Ruby SDKs, PostgreSQL, remote config, UI, local caching). Their verdict on Flagsmith: it "offers remote configuration but appears less polished with some features not working smoothly; Java SDK error reporting needs improvement."

Comparison from the same evaluation: Unleash was more powerful but lacked remote config, and Flipt lacked remote config and Java local caching. Flagsmith and FeatureHub both had remote config, but the user leaned toward FeatureHub because it also supports live data updates.
